title: Opposites Everywhere
objectives: I can say full and empty, and tell which is which.
I can use heavy, tall, and fast to describe things.
I can name the opposite of a describing word.
rationale: Opposite pairs are a fast way to deepen the meaning of a word, because children learn what a word is by what it is not. Full and empty are a pair for how much is inside; heavy, tall, and fast describe weight, height, and speed that children can feel and compare with real objects. Each word has a clear opposite (light, short, slow) that children can say even though it is not a target. The unit revisits different, quiet, and jump from earlier units.

words.def: Holding as much as it can hold.

words.ex2: My backpack is full of books.
words.nonExample: A cup with no water in it is not full.

words.def: Reaching high from bottom to top.

passage.title: Mia and the Apple Basket
paras: Mia and her tall brother Leo pick apples. Mia's basket is empty at first.
Soon it is full, and it is very heavy.
Leo is fast, so he runs to get the wagon. They lift the basket onto the wagon and roll it home.

qs.q: Mia's basket is empty at first. What is in it?
qs.why: Empty means nothing inside, so there is nothing in the basket at first.
The basket is full of apples, and a full basket of apples is hard to lift.

qs.q: Why does Leo run to get the wagon?
qs.why: Leo is fast, so he can bring the wagon quickly.

teacher.overview: Children learn five describing words by comparing real objects, such as full and empty cups and heavy and light bags. They hear the words in a short story about picking apples and say them in short sentences. Everything is oral.

notes.va.full.adj: Use clear cups and water, and let children pour. Full means no more room, so stop pouring at the top. Children may call a cup half full by the word full, so show a nearly full cup too.
notes.va.empty.adj: Hold up a box and look inside together. Empty means nothing inside, not broken or unused. Pair with full right away so children hear the pair.
notes.va.heavy.adj: Use two bags, one with books and one with paper, and let children lift both. Heavy is about weight, not size; a big pillow can be light, so show one.
notes.va.tall.adj: Compare a tower of blocks and a single block, then children against a wall chart. Tall is about height; do not use it for width. The opposite is short, which children can say.
notes.va.fast.adj: Move a toy car fast and slow. Fast means moving quickly. The word also has other meanings, such as holding tight or not eating, which are not taught here.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I pour milk into my cup. It is almost to the top, so it is full. Now I drink it all. Look inside. Nothing is there. The cup is empty. Say it with me: full, empty.'
discuss: What is a different way to say the opposite of heavy?
What is the tallest thing in our room?
extend: Make an opposites chart with picture pairs: full and empty, tall and short, heavy and light, fast and slow.
Play a lifting game with bags of different weights and ask children to say heavy or light.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit different, quiet, and jump by comparing pairs: How are full and empty different? Show a quiet and a loud jump. Use heavy and tall again in unit 10 when children describe plants growing tall.

frames: A ___ is heavy, but a ___ is light.
The ___ is tall, and the ___ is short.
wida.oral: Partner A says a describing word, such as heavy. Partner B says its opposite, such as light, and both say a sentence with one of the words.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (lleno, vacío, pesado, alto, rápido) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; alto also means loud in some regions and rápido is not a cognate of fast.
Sense boundary: fast is taught only as moving quickly; fast as firmly fixed or as not eating is left out.
Sense boundary: full is taught as holding as much as it can; the eating sense (my tummy is full) appears in one example.
Opposites light, short, and slow are named in ant lists and teacher text but are not targets in this unit.
